reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage:
Rising temperatures across the globe are changing more than just the weather. In the past decade, scientists have documented shifts in animal migration patterns, plant flowering times, and ocean chemistry that would once have taken centuries to unfold. What makes the current wave of change so alarming is not merely its scale, but its speed.

A growing body of research suggests that many species, particularly those in polar and mountain regions, may be unable to adapt fast enough. Coral reefs, which support roughly a quarter of all marine life, have already suffered mass bleaching events in three of the past six years. Meanwhile, communities of people living along low-lying coasts are being forced to consider relocation as sea levels creep upward.

Governments have responded with a patchwork of pledges to reduce emissions, but critics argue that these promises are rarely matched by concrete policy. The gap between rhetoric and action, they say, is where the next generation of environmental damage will be written.

Optimists point to rapid advances in clean energy technology as reason for hope. Solar power, once prohibitively expensive, is now the cheapest source of new electricity in most of the world. Whether such technologies can be deployed at the necessary scale — and quickly enough — remains an open question.

questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, what most concerns scientists about current climate change?
options: A) The scale of the changes
B) The speed of the changes
C) The variety of ecosystems affected
D) The difficulty of documenting the changes
questions.explanation: 首段末句明确指出 'not merely its scale, but its speed'，说明科学家最担心的是变化的速度。

questions.stem: The mention of coral reefs in paragraph 2 serves mainly to

questions.explanation: 作者以珊瑚礁 'mass bleaching events' 为例，说明海洋生态系统的脆弱。

questions.stem: The critics referred to in paragraph 3 believe that governments
options: A) have made too few pledges
B) fail to enforce their pledges

questions.explanation: critics 认为承诺 'rarely matched by concrete policy'——即政府并未落实。

questions.stem: What is the author's attitude toward clean energy technology?
questions.explanation: 末段先肯定 solar 变便宜，随后以 'remains an open question' 保留态度——审慎乐观。

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as waiters. In the early 2010s, a wide range of business started processing payments with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped. Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service provided, nor are they always presented after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after paying a barber or once a plane has landed. And new tipping technology may automatically add tips. The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tipping crept into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely use suggestions of default tips—often well above what they would have given in cash. The amounts have risen from 10% or 15% in the 1970s to around 20% today. This increase coincides with the rise of digital tipping, even though inflation has eroded the value of tips. Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped service jobs, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as $2.13 an hour. Tip and wage inflation have benefited some of these workers, such as cooks and dishwashers. Notably, primarily benefits some of these workers, not all. To ensure that all employees are paid fair wages, many employers are responding to tipping inflation by raising fixed prices, rather than increasing employees' pay. As a result, many customers feel they are being forced to pay a high cost of living, and other employees end up bearing the burden of tipping inflation. However, many customers, as our research emphasizes, tipping creates a more service-oriented culture and often completes difficult services.

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely free care to meet the dominant needs of the population at its creation. Nearly 75 years on, the UK is facing very different health challenges, it is clear that the old model is out of date. From life expectancy to infant and overall mortality rates, we are lagging badly compared with other wealthy nations. It is becoming increasingly unacceptable for us not to pay for private treatment or the cost of providing healthcare is becoming unsustainable for everyone, and growing pressure on the workforce—with daily staff break points—will continue to grow more acute. Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care will need to be embedded in communities and primary care, rather than simply be remedied at much more expensive hospitals and urgent care. That is why the NHS reform plan is not a new programme of reorganisation. Instead, the reform is supported by a new programme called "Reimagining health", supported by the voluntary sector and community groups. Its key idea is to shift care to the community and prevent poor health, rather than only treat illness. This must begin with prevention and social care, because only around 20% of our health outcomes are determined by clinical care, with 80% determined by wider social factors. Much more investment must go into prevention and social care to reduce the heavy price of treating illness, that reduces costs. Reforms want us to shift power and resources so that they can be given to local leaders, who are best positioned to understand the whole picture of their community, and build a much better understanding of their populations' conditions.

questions.stem: According to the first two paragraphs, the NHS ______.
options: A) is troubled by funding deficiencies

questions.explanation: 第二段指出英国面临的健康挑战与 NHS 成立时截然不同，旧模式已过时，在预期寿命和死亡率方面落后于其他国家，说明 NHS 很难满足人们的健康需求。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years. In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions. Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside "cold wards" in the summer months. But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research. Many lack adequate funding, it found. And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate. In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts. But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs. Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say. That day's high temperature of roughly 36℃ was 1℃ shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities. But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony. To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions. Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk. Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says. "A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters." For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings might be poorer with heat and could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers. The Nagpur project has already created a risk vulnerability map, and the city's HAP now includes tailored warnings. The project also includes long-term measures such as retrofitting homes to help reduce heat exposure. Kotharkar stresses that emergency response is only one part of the solution; the bigger goal is to reduce heat risk over the long term.

questions.stem: One problem with existing HAPs is that they ______.
options: A) prove too costly to be implemented
D) keep hospitals under persistent pressure
questions.explanation: 第三段指出触发阈值往往未针对当地气候定制，说明缺乏本地化的预警标准是现有热行动计划的问题。

questions.explanation: 第六段指出脆弱性地图可以帮助将应对措施聚焦于风险最高的人群，例如老年人多或非正式住房集中的社区，说明它可以有针对性地关注需要特殊照顾的区域。

questions.stem: It can be learned from the last paragraph that HAPs should ______.
options: A) focus more on heatstroke treatment
B) apply for more government grants
C) be updated on a regular basis
D) serve a broader range of purposes
questions.explanation: 末段指出紧急响应只是解决方案的一部分，更大的目标是长期减少热风险，说明热行动计划应服务于更广泛的目的（不仅限于应急响应）。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: Navigating the organised pavement and departure of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared contours and collective choices of human beings. Often appearing as narrow tracks through green spaces, these desire paths represent the natural capability of people and animals to go straight to point most effectively. Urban planners attempt to impose an official layout. Urban planners often intervene after visible informal pathways have been established. When planners overlook the desire paths, the cycle of creation, then pavement, then formal paving begins. The desire paths then become part of the official layout, gradually turning informal routes into permanent pavements. The Desirability Trail is an example of a historic desire path, created by massive settlements across the forests of Manhattan. These desire paths were gradually adopted as the main route across the island, which would become New York City. When the British established a grid street system in 1811, they ignored these desire paths. The grid pattern became the basis of the street system that defines Manhattan today. The desire paths were erased from the official layout, yet they persist in the public imagination and online forums, where they continue to fascinate urban explorers.

reading.title: Text 1
reading.passage: For thousands of years, donkeys have been critical for propelling human civilizations forward. They've helped pull wheeled vehicles, carry travelers and move goods across the world. But where and when these animals first became intertwined with humans has been a mystery. Now, researchers have used genomes of over 200 donkeys to trace their domestication back to a single event around 7,000 years ago in East Africa — about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses. The team published their findings in the journal Science this month. "Through their DNA, the animals are telling their history themselves," co-author Samantha Brooks, an equine researcher at the University of Florida, says in a statement. "We usually only get the human's side of history through written accounts, but of course written history does not always record exactly how something happened. Looking at these DNA sequences, we get a biological testimony to the environment these animals lived in and the experiences they survived." The researchers examined 207 genomes from modern donkeys living in 31 countries across the globe. They also looked at genomes from 15 wild equids and 31 earlier donkeys that lived between about 4,000 and 100 years ago. The team reconstructed the animals' evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when herders in Kenya and the Horn of Africa tamed wild asses. They then traced how the animals spread across the rest of the continent into Europe and Asia about 2,500 years later. Though it's still unclear why the original domestication happened, Science News' Freda Kreier reports that the event coincided with the Sahara growing larger and drier. "Donkeys are champions when it comes to carrying stuff and are good at crossing deserts," co-author Ludovic Orlando, an evolutionary biologist at Paul Sabatier University in France, tells the publication. Prehistoric humans may have tamed donkeys to help navigate the expanding Sahara. Researchers say these findings could help put donkeys in the spotlight. The animals could benefit from more research: Currently, there are no published genomes from donkeys located south of the Equator in Africa. But understanding where the animals were first domesticated could guide archaeologists to a narrow region to search for insights about the original tamed donkeys. Not only does understanding the equines' genetic makeup help reveal their contribution to human history, but it also might improve their management in the future, as climate change alters the planet's environment, write the authors.

questions.stem: What can be learned about donkeys from Paragraph 1?

questions.explanation: 第 21 题是细节题，正确答案 C）They were tamed at an earlier time than horses. 定位句在第 1 段：如今，研究者用 200 多份驴基因组将其驯化追溯到约 7000 年前东非的一次单一事件——比人类驯化马早约 3000 年。正确项与原文构成同义替换（about 3,000 years before humans tamed horses ↔ They were tamed at an earlier time than horses）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The authors think that their research could help with ____
options: C) recovering early types of donkeys.
D) raising awareness of climate change.
questions.explanation: 第 25 题是细节题，正确答案 B）better management of donkeys. 定位句在第 6 段：作者写道，理解这些马科动物的遗传构成不仅有助于揭示它们对人类历史的贡献，还可能在气候变化改变全球环境之际改善对它们的管理。正确项与原文构成同义替换（it also might improve their management in the future ↔ better management of donkeys）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属过度推断、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

reading.title: Text 2
reading.passage: There's no business like show business — but in Los Angeles, it feels like there's no business at all. If that sounds melodramatic, consider this: The Art Directors Guild, a labor union representing about 3,000 film workers, has suspended a training program and issued a statement explaining that "we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession." This is a reaction to Hollywood's decline, which is reaching a critical point for the industry and Southern California. Production has been slipping away from Hollywood since the 1950s, but the effects have never been more apparent than at present. Other regions in the United States, Canada and Europe have steadily increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies, leaving California in the dust. Georgia offers up to 30% in transferable tax credits on film and TV production costs, plus an additional 10% increase on the base tax credit if the project includes a Georgia promotional logo. Even as California lost a huge volume of production to other locations, there was still plenty of film production taking place in Los Angeles before this year. We were kept afloat by "peak TV", the glut of content that was required by the explosion of streaming services. But 2022 was the peak of peak TV. Back then platforms such as Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV hemorrhaged billions of dollars to generate content to attract new subscribers, resulting in 633 scripted series being released that year. As the streamers' emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability, prices for the services went up and the number of new shows went down to 481 released in 2023, with the number expected to dip into the 300s within a few years. If productions in Southern California dip below a critical level for too long, the industry's essential talent will drift away along with enormous sums of revenue. Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn't offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses that support the entertainment industry. That's why the California Film Commission and its Los Angeles counterpart, Film LA, now should act, before it's too late. These agencies and other government bodies should dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles. Let's go on with the show…and make sure the show doesn't go on without us.

questions.stem: The Art Directors Guild's statement reveals ____
options: A) people's reduced interest in film.
B) film workers' nostalgia for the past.
C) the appeal of Southern California.
D) the gloomy situation of Hollywood.
questions.explanation: 第 26 题是细节题，正确答案 D）the gloomy situation of Hollywood. 定位句在第 2 段：这是对好莱坞衰落的一种反应，这种衰落对该行业和南加州来说已达到临界点。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Hollywood's decline, which is reaching a critical point ↔ the gloomy situation of Hollywood；we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession ↔ the gloomy situation of Hollywood）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属无中生有、C 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: The example of Georgia is used to illustrate the efforts to ____

questions.explanation: 第 27 题是例证目的题，正确答案 A）lure production with tax incentives. 定位句在第 3 段：美国、加拿大和欧洲的其他地区一直在稳步加大激励力度，以吸引电视剧和电影制作，把加州甩在身后。佐治亚州对影视制作成本提供高达 30% 的可转让税收抵免，如果项目中包含佐治亚州的宣传标志，还可在基础税收抵免上再加 10%。正确项与原文构成同义替换（increased incentives to attract TV shows and movies ↔ lure production with tax incentives）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属过度推断、D 项属偷换概念，均可排除。

questions.stem: Peak TV passed its peak as ____
options: A) streamers lost their technical advantages.
B) streamers changed their strategic priorities.
C) subscribers grew wary of large platforms.
D) subscribers were unhappy with new shows.
questions.explanation: 第 28 题是细节题，正确答案 B）streamers changed their strategic priorities. 定位句在第 5 段：随着流媒体的重心从用户增长转向盈利能力，服务价格上涨，新剧数量下降至 2023 年的 481 部，预计未来几年将进一步跌入 300 多部区间。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the streamers' emphasis changed from subscriber growth to profitability ↔ streamers changed their strategic priorities）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属张冠李戴、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 6, California's entertainment industry might face ____
options: A) a decline in product quality.
B) a demand for foreign talent.
C) a brain drain to other places.

questions.explanation: 第 29 题是细节题，正确答案 C）a brain drain to other places. 定位句在第 6 段：如果南加州的影视制作量长期低于临界水平，行业的核心人才将与巨额收入一起流失。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the industry's essential talent will drift away ↔ a brain drain to other places；Persuading studios to film here would become much more challenging if we couldn't offer a deep bench of local film workers, on-screen talent and local businesses ↔ a brain drain to other places）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The author concludes the text by emphasizing that California should strive to ____

questions.explanation: 第 30 题是主旨题，正确答案 A）maintain its position in the industry. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（make sure the show doesn't go on without us ↔ maintain its position in the industry；dramatically improve incentives to keep our current shows and attract new productions to Los Angeles ↔ maintain its position in the industry）。其余三项中，B 项属偷换概念、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

reading.title: Text 3
reading.passage: The pioneers of wireless saw it as a gift to all the people. Sir John Reith said that it would end "isolation of the spirit" and rejoiced: "It does not matter how many thousands may be listening, there is always enough for others…the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously." Between two great wars this technological innovation built a new kind of national consciousness. Opening this week, a book and exhibition curated by Beatty Rubens at the Bodleian in Oxford records how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939. She draws on letters, diaries and fiction, and a 1939 field notebook of verbatim audience research by Winifred Gill. There's fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness. A cartoon mocks a group failing to converse because they're all in headphones. People report that broadcast music made workmen whistle new tunes. A woman says there have been fewer street fights since the arrival of the wireless but also less stopping and "talking on the brush handle". By and large the wireless was welcome. I loved the man from the Thirties research who found that wireless suddenly offered "a lot of variety…things I thought I'd never be interested in…ice hockey perhaps". True: for more than 80 pre-digital years, linear speech broadcasting brought the gift of serendipity, random enlivening of a car journey or dull manual task. In my own book about radio I recorded how, on one drive: "I caught up with the news, learnt some 17th-century history, and was startlingly educated by an unpretentious programme on the history of the stethoscope." But radio's enriching serendipity is ebbing. With multiple networks and countless podcasts, a smartphone user selects what to hear and when. And while it is wonderful to take a walk with anything in your headphones, infinite choice encourages us to shrink into niche interests and sympathetic beliefs. A hundred years on from Marconi and Reith, is the art of mere listening endangered? Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading. But inventions shape all of us and it is worth noticing when techno-social habits do change, and asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest. Whatever we do, innovation will happen. Today we fret about the isolating culture of smartphone-staring and selfie-vanity, but already in 1939 there was that lady regretting how, when all her street got wirelesses, it lost the neighbourly habit of "talking on the brush handle". It's enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.

questions.stem: What can be learnt about wireless from Sir John Reith?
options: A) It was accessible to everyone.
C) It was a miracle of human ingenuity.
D) It led to a new era of isolating culture.
questions.explanation: 第 31 题是细节题，正确答案 A）It was accessible to everyone. 定位句在第 1 段：约翰·里斯爵士说，无线电会结束"精神上的孤立"，并欣然表示："无论有多少千人在收听都没关系，永远有足够的份额留给其他人……天才与傻瓜、富人与穷人可以同时收听。"正确项与原文构成同义替换（the genius and the fool, the wealthy and the poor listen simultaneously ↔ accessible to everyone；there is always enough for others ↔ accessible）。其余三项中，B 项属无中生有、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What is the theme of the exhibition at the Bodleian in Oxford?
options: A) The impact of radio on its early audience.
B) The role of radio in public music education.
C) The innovation process of radio technology.
D) The eminent pioneers in radio broadcasting.
questions.explanation: 第 32 题是细节题，正确答案 A）The impact of radio on its early audience. 定位句在第 2 段：本周开幕、由 Beatty Rubens 在牛津 Bodleian 图书馆策划的一本书及一场展览，记录了 1922 年至 1939 年间无线电如何改变了日常生活。正确项与原文构成同义替换（how radio changed everyday life from 1922 to 1939 ↔ The impact of radio on its early audience）。其余三项中，B 项属以偏概全、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: It is indicated in Paragraph 4 that ____
options: A) the research on radio used to be inadequate.
B) the charm of radio remains in the digital age.
C) radio listeners could make unexpected gains.
D) radio shows have changed little over the years.
questions.explanation: 第 33 题是细节题，正确答案 C）radio listeners could make unexpected gains. 定位句在第 4 段：在数字时代之前的八十多年里，线性的语音广播带来了"意外发现"的礼物——它能随机点亮一段乏味的开车旅程或无聊的体力劳动。正确项与原文构成同义替换（the gift of serendipity ↔ unexpected gains；things I thought I'd never be interested in…ice hockey perhaps ↔ unexpected）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

questions.stem: The expression "talking on the brush handle" in Paragraphs 3 and 6 refers to the act of ____
questions.explanation: 第 34 题是词义句意题，正确答案 B）having a casual chat. 定位句在第 3 段：一位女士说，自从无线电出现以来，街头打架变少了，但也少了人们驻足在扫帚柄上闲聊的情景。正确项与原文构成同义替换（less stopping and "talking on the brush handle" ↔ having a casual chat；lost the neighbourly habit of "talking on the brush handle" ↔ casual chat）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、C 项属偷换概念、D 项属张冠李戴，均可排除。

questions.stem: In the last paragraph, the author intends to express the opinion that ____

B) actions should be taken to revive the art of listening.

D) people should adopt a sensible attitude to innovations.
questions.explanation: 第 35 题是主旨题，正确答案 D）people should adopt a sensible attitude to innovations. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（asking whether to control them a bit or shield the youngest ↔ a sensible attitude to innovations；innovation will happen ↔ innovations）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属以偏概全、C 项属以偏概全，均可排除。

reading.title: Text 4
reading.passage: When Tom Swetnam joined the U.S. Forest Service in the 1970s, his mandate was to "put everything out," he recalled. But when Swetnam enrolled in graduate school at the University of Arizona's Laboratory of Tree-Ring Research, he was surprised to find a record of repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent. Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings. The fact that fires happened so often meant they couldn't have been severe enough to kill most trees. Instead, a growing body of research showed that frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier. They rid the forest of dead and sick trees, reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease. Because flammable material couldn't build up on the landscape, blazes tended to move slowly and peter out when they reached the footprints of previous burns. In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent. Their North American tree-ring fire-scar network (NAFSN) provided the basis for a study published last month. In the study, the researchers compared the historical fire cadence with the wildfires recorded over the past few decades, and uncovered a striking shortfall. The NAFSN sites experienced less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected without fire suppression. This deficit is a testament to the effectiveness of modern firefighting, said Kelly Martin, a past president of the International Association of Wildland Fire. "Yet the combined consequences of suppression and climate change have eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires, particularly those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions." To prevent entire ecosystems from going up in smoke, Martin said, people must bring healthy fire back to places that need it. At Yosemite National Park, Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient. These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and helped eliminate some of the fuel that had built up around the important park's facilities. Research shows that these prescribed burns make subsequent wildfires less severe, even if later fires happen under the most dangerous weather conditions. Yet even as scientists and public officials increasingly agree on the need for more fires in our forests, climate change is making this tactic more challenging, experts said. "It's a double-edged sword because wildfires are getting more severe and larger under climate change and we need this work even more, but then the work gets more challenging," said Susan Prichard, a fire ecologist at the University of Washington.

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Swetnam was surprised by ____
options: A) the scarcity of tree-ring research in the U.S.
B) the firefighting measures in ancient Europe.
C) the forest management practices in the 1970s.
D) the number of wildfires in precolonial times.
questions.explanation: 第 36 题是细节题，正确答案 D）the number of wildfires in precolonial times. 定位句在第 1 段：但是当 Swetnam 进入亚利桑那大学树轮研究室读研时，他惊讶地发现一份记录显示，早在欧洲殖民者抵达这片大陆几百年前就已存在反复发生的火灾。正确项与原文构成同义替换（repeated blazes dating back hundreds of years before European colonists arrived on the continent ↔ the number of wildfires in precolonial times；Some of the trees he analyzed bore more than 20 fire scars among their rings. ↔ the number of wildfires in precolonial times）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属偷换概念、C 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: Paragraph 2 mainly focuses on ____
options: A) the causes of previous burns.
B) the treatment of diseased trees.
C) the benefits of low-severity fires.
D) the importance of forest ecosystems.
questions.explanation: 第 37 题是主旨题，正确答案 C）the benefits of low-severity fires. 定位句在第 2 段：相反，越来越多的研究表明，频繁、低强度的火灾让许多生态系统更健康。正确项与原文构成同义替换（frequent, low-severity fires made many ecosystems healthier ↔ the benefits of low-severity fires.；reducing competition and curbing the spread of disease ↔ the benefits of low-severity fires.）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属以偏概全、D 项属答非所问，均可排除。

questions.stem: What did the study find about the wildfires over the past few decades?
options: A) Their intensity has vastly fluctuated.
B) Their frequency has markedly decreased.
C) Their threats have been underestimated.
D) Their records have been misinterpreted.
questions.explanation: 第 38 题是细节题，正确答案 B）Their frequency has markedly decreased. 定位句在第 3 段：在这项研究中，研究者把历史上的火灾节律与近几十年记录的野火相比较，发现了一个惊人的缺口：NAFSN 各站点经历的火灾数量不到原本（在没有灭火措施时）应当出现数量的四分之一。正确项与原文构成同义替换（less than a quarter of the number of fires that would have been expected ↔ Their frequency has markedly decreased.；uncovered a striking shortfall ↔ Their frequency has markedly decreased.）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、C 项属无中生有、D 项属与原文相反，均可排除。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about modern firefighting?
options: A) Its workforce needs more training.
B) Its effectiveness is questioned by the public.
C) It may render traditional tactics useless.
D) It may make severe fires harder to put out.
questions.explanation: 第 39 题是推断题，正确答案 D）It may make severe fires harder to put out. 定位句在第 4 段：然而，灭火措施与气候变化的共同后果已经削弱了人类压制火灾的能力——尤其是那些在最危险天气条件下被点燃的火。正确项与原文构成同义替换（eroded humanity's ability to suppress fires ↔ It may make severe fires harder to put out.；those that ignite under the most dangerous weather conditions ↔ It may make severe fires harder to put out.）。其余三项中，A 项属无中生有、B 项属与原文相反、C 项属过度推断，均可排除。

questions.stem: Both Martin and Prichard would agree that ____
options: A) it is challenging to predict large wildfires.
B) it is urgent to assess the use of planned fires.
C) it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.
D) it is rewarding to double fire detection efforts.
questions.explanation: 第 40 题是态度题，正确答案 C）it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns. 该题需通观全文作答。正确项与原文构成同义替换（Martin oversaw the use of what is known as prescribed burns to make the landscape more resilient ↔ it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.；we need this work even more ↔ it is necessary to introduce prescribed burns.）。其余三项中，A 项属偷换概念、B 项属偷换概念、D 项属无中生有，均可排除。

blanks.explanation: 第 1 空正确答案 A）Still。前句赞美、后句揭隐患——典型转折。其余三项：B）Therefore 因果方向反了、C）Afterward 时序词，与语义无关、D）Instead 替代义过强，会否定前句，均可排除。
第 2 空正确答案 D）dominating。hazard + difficult to control 锁定"强势主导"义。其余三项：A）reviewing 动作太弱，不足以构成 hazard、B）narrating "叙述"与体验不搭、C）ignoring 方向相反——忽略反而无影响，均可排除。
第 3 空正确答案 B）area。上一句提到的是"难以控制的体验范围"。其余三项：A）reason 下文没有给出原因、C）clue "线索"语义与论证结构无关、D）belief "信念"与下文"理解和体验美"不对应，均可排除。
第 4 空正确答案 C）Combining。上一句的 collaborative 已经给出方向。其余三项：A）Balancing "平衡"偏取舍，不强调融合、B）Distinguishing "区分"方向相反、D）Introducing "引入"宾语单选，无双方互动，均可排除。
第 5 空正确答案 B）outcomes。lead to + beautiful to the human eye 锁定"产物"义。其余三项：A）prospects "前景"是未来期望，不是现成产物、C）ambitions "野心"属内心意图，非视觉产物、D）sentiments "情感"指主观感受，非作品本身，均可排除。
第 6 空正确答案 C）For instance。上句给"艺术协作"作例，本句给"虚拟试妆"作另一例。其余三项：A）At first "起初"暗示时间序，无对应、B）By comparison "相比之下"需要对比反差、D）In general "总的来说"应用于段尾总结，均可排除。
第 7 空正确答案 A）test。try-on + virtually 锁定"试"义。其余三项：B）copy "复制"不符合用户体验逻辑、C）link "连接"与试用无关、D）save "保存"在前置体验逻辑里太靠后，均可排除。
第 8 空正确答案 D）before。virtual try-on 与 physical changes 是"试在前、改在后"。其余三项：A）upon "一……就"指紧接发生、B）beyond "超出"范围义不通、C）through "通过"会把因果颠倒，均可排除。
第 9 空正确答案 A）explore。experiment + expanding the range 共指"探索"义。其余三项：B）recall "回忆"是回看已有，方向相反、C）simplify "简化"与"扩展"相反、D）cherish "珍视"是情感动作，不是试用结果，均可排除。

第 12 空正确答案 D）In this way。前文铺垫已具备"个性化分析→自我发现"的因果链。其余三项：A）At best "充其量"含贬抑色彩，与正面结论冲突、B）To the contrary "相反地"需要反向论点、C）By definition "按定义"需要定义性命题，均可排除。
第 13 空正确答案 C）concerns。while + raises 锁定"伦理担忧"义。其余三项：A）divisions "分歧"虽偏负面，但与 raise 不搭、B）expectations "期待"色彩偏正面、D）values "价值观"被引发不通，均可排除。
第 14 空正确答案 A）pressures。perpetuating unattainable beauty standards 锁定"审美压力"。其余三项：B）mysteries "神秘"中性偏褒，方向不对、C）understandings "理解"是正向认知，加剧后矛盾、D）suspicions "怀疑"色彩虽负面但不对位，均可排除。
第 15 空正确答案 B）Additionally。上下两句都是"AI 带来负面效应"的并列。其余三项：A）Approximately "大约"用于数量近似、C）Alternatively "或者说"暗示替代选项、D）Accidentally "偶然地"与系统性现象冲突，均可排除。
第 16 空正确答案 C）contribute to。并列 distorted self-perception 决定方向。其余三项：A）deal with "处理"方向相反、B）result from "由……产生"主从因果倒置、D）focus on "聚焦于"与因果无关，均可排除。
第 17 空正确答案 C）relying。for social presentation + cause harm 锁定"依赖"义。其余三项：A）starting "开始"与 cause harm 因果太弱、B）checking "检查"语义与社交呈现无关、D）working "运作"主语不对，均可排除。
